top_stories.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervention; Bitcoin Rallies
points: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just 6 days after reversing an earlier decision against his return, citing 'input from senior levels of the United States government.'

Nvidia shares jumped 31% in a single day, from $125.53 to $164 (intraday high $171.50), adding over $36 billion to Huang's net worth and costing short sellers (investors who bet on a stock's price falling) an estimated $12 billion.
Trump claimed credit for the reversal, telling CNBC 'I made the deal' and saying the board received government-level security assurances.

Congress is demanding investigations into Huang's reinstatement and high-end chip sales to China; Huang faces closed-door hearings before three House committees on December 1 plus a Senate summons, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick also called to testify.
Bitcoin rallied following a prior selloff as risk appetite returned to crypto markets alongside the Nvidia surge.

unique_angles.point: Decrypt's prediction market gives Nvidia only 3% odds of reaching $216 by end-November, suggesting limited near-term upside despite the rally.
Anthropic's fresh IPO underperformed amid the Nvidia surge and broader market shifts.
Lawmakers Don Bacon (R-NE) and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) both demanded answers on who approved high-end chip exports to China.
Bitcoin's price specifically reached $63,644 in the rally following the Huang news.

items.title: Strategy Boosts Bitcoin Holdings and Buyback Program
points: Michael Saylor's Strategy firm bought $30 million in additional Bitcoin.
The company increased its stock buyback program to $4 billion and moved $1 billion from USD reserves into its cash pool.

items.title: Cross River Bank Launches Bitcoin-Backed Loans
points: Cross River Bank introduced bitcoin-backed loan products for fintech partners and their customers, expanding access to crypto-collateralized lending.

headlines: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump intervened, citing national security assurances; Nvidia shares surged 31% in a single day, adding $36 billion to Huang's wealth while short sellers lost $12 billion.
Trump claimed credit for the CEO reinstatement, telling CNBC 'I made the deal' and providing the board with government-level security assurances that enabled the decision.

Congress is demanding answers on Huang's return, with lawmakers from both parties vowing investigations into high-end chip sales to China; Huang faces three House committee hearings on December 1 and a Senate summons.
Bitcoin rallied after a punishing selloff following Huang's reinstatement, while Anthropic's fresh IPO underperformed amid the Nvidia surge and broader market shifts.
Michael Saylor's Strategy firm bought $30 million in Bitcoin and increased its stock buyback program to $4 billion, moving $1 billion from USD reserves to cash.

sections.title: The Huang Reinstatement and Market Impact
points: Nvidia's board unanimously reversed its November 17 decision against Huang's return within just 6 days, explicitly citing 'input from senior levels of the United States government' as the determining factor.
Huang's net worth surged over $36 billion as Nvidia stock jumped from $125.53 (Friday close) to $164 by market close, with an intraday high of $171.50—a 31% single-day gain.
Short sellers suffered estimated $12 billion in losses from the reversal, while Bitcoin rallied from a selloff as risk appetite returned to crypto markets.
Despite the stock surge, Decrypt's prediction market gives Nvidia only 3% odds of reaching $216 by end-November, suggesting limited near-term upside despite current momentum.

sections.title: Congressional Oversight and Regulatory Scrutiny
points: Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) both demanded Congress investigate who approved high-end computer chip sales to China, signaling bipartisan concern about exports.
Huang is scheduled to testify before three House committees behind closed doors on December 1, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick also summoned by Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott (R-SC).
The reinstatement does not resolve underlying export control questions about Nvidia's sales to China and the degree of government involvement in CEO personnel decisions.
Lawmakers indicated investigations into chip exports and Huang's reinstatement timing will continue regardless of his return to the CEO role.
